title: 3 Seoul Spots Every Esports Fan Should Visit: GGX, T1 Base Camp, and CHZZK LoL Park
html:
South Korea is often called the "esports capital of the world" — this is the country that invented the PC bang (PC방, literally "computer room," a pay-by-the-hour gaming cafe) and still produces some of the best professional League of Legends players on the planet. You don't need to be a hardcore gamer to enjoy this side of Korea. Here are three spots in Seoul — a cultural gaming hub, a pro team's fan lounge, and the actual arena where pro matches are played — that you can visit on their own, in any order, without building a whole multi-day itinerary around them.

A quick heads-up: gaming venues in Korea open, rebrand, and close faster than most tourist attractions — the pro league's own arena changed its name partway through 2025. Treat the hours and prices below as a solid starting point, but it's worth a quick search or a check on Naver Map (Korea's most accurate local map app) the night before your visit.

Gen.G GGX — A Huge Cultural Gaming Hub in Dongdaemun

GGX (short for "Gen.G Gaming Xperience") is a massive public gaming hall run by Gen.G, one of Korea's biggest esports organizations. It opened in June 2025 right next to Dongdaemun History & Culture Park Station (subway lines 2, 4, and 5) — the same stop you'd use for the famous DDP building. The space covers about 1,570 square meters with 252 gaming stations, plus a food and drink lounge, a merchandise shop, and photo zones with the team mascot.

GGX was built to welcome foreign visitors as well as local fans, so don't feel shy about walking in without a Korean-speaking friend — look for an English option at the entrance kiosk. Exact hourly pricing isn't officially published, so check the venue's Instagram (@geng_ggx) or a booking site like Klook for the current rate before you go. One fun detail: GGX and the T1 lounge below are both run by the same operating company, Superplay, which is why the two venues feel like siblings.


Dongdaemun Design Plaza, right next to the same subway station you'll use to reach GGX. Photo: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 — source.

T1 Base Camp — Step Into a Pro Team's World in Hongdae

T1 Base Camp is a gaming lounge run by T1, the esports team behind the world-famous League of Legends player Faker. The original location is at 147 Yanghwa-ro, Mapo-gu, a short walk from Hongik University Station Exit 1, and it's open 24 hours. It's part PC bang, part fan museum: premium gaming PCs, a merchandise shop, a lounge area, and big screens that show T1's matches live when the team is playing.

You don't need to sign up for anything in advance — walk-ins are normal. Non-member, tourist-rate pricing is reportedly around ₩3,000 per hour (roughly double the rate a Korean regular pays with a membership), though this figure comes from a single source, so confirm it on-site or on Naver Map. T1 has since opened a second, larger Base Camp in Gangnam and another in Busan, so if Hongdae doesn't fit your route, you have other options.


A street in Hongdae, the neighborhood where T1 Base Camp's original location is based. Photo: U0894629, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

CHZZK LoL Park — Watch a Pro Match Live, Right by Jonggak Station

If you want to see Korean esports at the highest level, head to CHZZK LoL Park (renamed from "LoL Park" in late 2025, after a streaming platform called CHZZK), the dedicated arena where Korea's professional League of Legends league — the LCK — plays its official matches. It's on the 3rd floor of Tower 1 in the Gran Seoul building, about a 1-minute walk from Jonggak Station Exit 1 (subway line 1).

The venue is small — seating only around 400–450 people — so tickets for live matches sell out fast. General seats typically run ₩25,000–35,000, bookable through the NOL or Interpark ticketing apps/sites; check the current LCK match schedule before you plan your trip, since matches aren't held every day. The building is open 11:00–20:00 daily, stretching later on match days until the final game ends. Even without a match on, the exhibition area is sometimes open to walk through for free — just confirm the hours on Naver Map first, since they can vary.


Jongno Tower, a well-known landmark right by Jonggak Station, near the Gran Seoul building where CHZZK LoL Park is located. Photo: Schölla Schwarz, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

Which One Should You Visit?

All three are easy subway rides apart, so you can hit more than one in a single day if you want:

VenueLocationTypical priceBest for
Gen.G GGXDongdaemun History & Culture Park StationNot officially published — check Instagram/KlookA big, modern gaming hall with photo spots and merch
T1 Base CampHongik Univ. Station Exit 1 (Hongdae)~₩3,000/hr for non-members (unconfirmed, single source)Faker and T1 fans, a casual PC bang try-out
CHZZK LoL ParkJonggak Station Exit 1₩25,000–35,000 per match ticketWatching Korea's top pro league play live

💬 Planning a gaming-themed day in Seoul, or have a question about any of these spots? Drop it in the comments — happy to help!
meta_description: A beginner's guide to 3 Seoul esports spots: Gen.G GGX, T1 Base Camp, and CHZZK LoL Park, where Korea's pro league plays.
